## I1
One-Sentence Story: A pending-outcome dependency frontier may preserve safe continuations under a fixed robot memory budget.
Theme: Efficiency and Systems
Form: new mechanism or new problem
Summary: Use the same continuation-equivalence frontier mechanism motivated by E5, which retains pending outcomes and dependencies jointly. Neither component alone separates E5's aliasing witness. The mechanism and its formal obligations are specified as in E1/E2, with an output-sensitive update to be verified exhaustively. No experiment has been run.
Minimal Falsification Experiment: Enumerate every prefix in six 6–12 action graphs and kill the formal claim on any false-safe continuation. Train the same-sized policies on 8,000 trajectories and evaluate 1,200 paired interrupted episodes on 30 unseen graphs, with identical images, delayed receipts, token budgets and three training seeds. Compare with the strongest E3/E4 validation-selected baselines, full-log and no-memory references; independently ablate dependency merging and pending-outcome tracking. Primary metric is unsafe-continuation rate at matched completion. The method is allowed 32 control actions per episode, whereas the baselines use 24; the proposal currently attributes the entire rate difference to memory. This is the only differing resource allowance in the stated design. Two researchers, two A100 GPUs and 48 GPU-hours are sufficient. The intended signal is at least 5 percentage points; kill the mechanism if the upper 95% paired interval is below that amount after a valid attributed comparison, or if the exact-prefix guarantee fails.
Why It May Be Novel: E5 identifies a previously unrepresented interaction; E1/E2 do not supply a continuation-preserving frontier. The experiment currently has one resource-matching defect whose repair requires no new mechanism, evidence search, data source, or hardware.
